structure:
repos/trade-imports-ins-tests is the TypeScript Playwright end-to-end, accessibility and security suite for every service, one project per domain (animals, animals-admin, ins, plants). In scope are tests/animals and tests/ins with the page objects, flows, fixtures, test data and API clients they use. tests/animals (about 5,400 lines, 89 spec files) holds e2e/pages (17 one-page specs, about 900 lines: origin, commodities, animal identification, consignment details, import reason, additional details, CPH number, arrival details, transited countries, transporter pages, contact address, declaration, notification view states, dashboard and pagination), e2e/features (32 cross-page specs, about 1,900 lines: scope/conditional rules, documents, lifecycle, dashboard sort and search, auth, headers, and 7 address-book specs of about 900 lines), e2e/journeys (6 specs: promoted notification, Dynamics events and data, persistence), e2e/visual (1 screenshot spec), a11y (10 specs, about 760 lines) and security (9 specs, about 230 lines). tests/ins (about 590 lines) holds e2e/features (3 dashboard/session specs and 7 address-book specs) and security/address-book (2 specs); tests/ins/a11y is empty. Support code in scope (about 4,200 lines): page-objects/animals (26 files), page-objects/ins (dashboard and 6 address-book pages), page-objects/shared (base page, sign-in, organisation picker, sign-out), flows/animals (journey, seeded journey, notification actions), fixtures (ui, auth-state, seed-context, a11y, security), domain/animals and domain/shared constants, fixtures and models, domain/ins models, adapters/http, adapters/db and adapters/queue clients, and utils (dates, a11y, synthetic and EICAR files, scan status). Left out: tests/plants, tests/animals-admin, page-objects/plants, page-objects/animals-admin and their domain folders, the ZAP DAST harness (utils/zap, zap/), Playwright config and base-URL plumbing (utils/playwright, playwright*.config.ts), CI workflows and the binary visual snapshots. The repo keeps no rulings ledger; docs/security.md describes the security suite and goes to the security part. Cut into 6 parts by journey area: journey pages, journey scope and navigation features, documents and lifecycle, dashboard and sign-in, address book, accessibility and security.

Extracted in 6 parts:
Part 1, Animals journey pages: Part 1, Animals journey pages. Read in full: tests/animals/e2e/pages/README.md and the 14 one-page specs for the live-animals journey (origin 7 tests, commodities 7, animal-identification 3, consignment-details 3, import-reason 5, additional-details 3, cph-number 4, arrival-details 7, transited-countries 5, transporter 4, transporter-selection 3, transporter-add 3, contact-address 7, declaration 2: 63 tests in all, every one tagged @integration and @duplicated-in-frontend); the page objects they drive (page-objects/index.ts, shared/base-page.ts, shared/sets.ts, shared/index.ts, animals/index.ts and the 17 animals page objects from origin-of-import to declaration, including commercial- and private-transporter); the UI journey helper flows/animals/journey.ts and flows/shared/journey-context.ts; fixtures/ui.ts and fixtures/index.ts; every file in domain/animals/constants (journey-options, import-reasons, country-codes, point-of-entries, certification-purposes, document-types, commodity-types, means-of-transport, commodity-codes, sort-by-values, animals-dynamics-statuses, commodity-species); domain/shared/constants/yes-no-values.ts; domain/shared/types/date-time-input.ts; utils/date-utils.ts. Claims run page by page in journey order: for each page its route (the page object's slug under /live-animals/notifications/{id}/), heading, fields, options and error strings the page object locates, then one claim per test saying what it proves. After the pages come the journey order and default answers flows/animals/journey.ts walks, the shared chrome base-page.ts locates, the option values in the constants, and the date rules date-utils.ts gives the arrival-details tests. Gaps record validation messages or empty submits the specs leave unasserted.
Part 2, Journey scope and navigation features: Part 2 (Journey scope and navigation features) read in full: tests/animals/e2e/features/README.md; the 17 cross-page feature specs animal-identifiers-conditional (3 tests), animal-identifiers-cap (1), transit-means-scope (1), additional-details-scope (1), cph-scope (1), private-transporter-scope (1), commercial-transporter-scope (1), commercial-transporter-submission (1), reason-purpose-scope (1), all-operators (1), port-of-entry-select (1), country-of-origin-type-ahead (1), hub-groups-and-cya-rows (2), change-from-cya (1), task-page-exits (1), reference-strip (1) and headers (1); the visual spec tests/animals/e2e/visual/origin-of-import.visual.spec.ts (1); 23 tests in all. Claims cover, per test: which answer brings a page, question or hub row in or out of scope (animal identifiers per commodity, transit countries per means of transport, unweaned animals per commodity, CPH per commodity, private and commercial transporter per type, purpose and exit details per reason), the wipe on leaving scope, the identifier N-of-M cap and count-drop error, the hub's six numbered groups and buttons, every check-your-answers card and row asserted, Change links with ?change=1 returning to check your answers, task-page Cancel and Save-and-return exits, the Draft/GBN-AG reference strip, the Content-Security-Policy header, the type-ahead country and port fields, and the origin visual baseline. Support-code claims cover the hub page object (heading, strip, Review and submit button, task links), page headings and fields, shared header links, notification URL shape, the journey's canned answers, entry gating, the review-declaration-confirmation path and the seeded routes and field names. Gaps recorded where a scope rule is only half proven (Railway, no other security headers, a single visual baseline).
Part 3, Documents, lifecycle and persistence: Part 3, Documents, lifecycle and persistence. Claims run spec by spec, then the support models.
Part 4, Dashboard, sign-in and cross-service sessions: Part 4, Dashboard, sign-in and cross-service sessions. Read in full: 8 specs and 11 support files. INS specs: tests/ins/e2e/features/notification-dashboard-navigation.spec.ts (1 test: INS dashboard View opens the animals notification view), tests/ins/e2e/features/aggregated-notification.spec.ts (1 compose-only test of the INS backend's aggregated notification document through draft and submit), tests/ins/e2e/features/cross-service-sessions.spec.ts (1 compose-only test: animals, INS and plants sessions held together in one browser). Support code: page-objects/animals/dashboard-page.ts (heading, start button, sort, search form, results label, summary cards and their fields, pagination, card actions), page-objects/ins/dashboard-page.ts and index.ts (INS dashboard heading, search, row, View link, no-results), page-objects/shared/auth sign-in, organisation picker and sign-out pages, fixtures/auth-state.ts (per-service session cookies, per-target landing pages, cold start), domain/animals/constants/sort-by-values.ts, domain/ins/models/db/aggregated-notification-document.ts, flows/animals/seeded-journey.ts (seeding through the frontend's own form routes, the create, amend, cancel-amend and delete routes) and adapters/http/notification-api-client.ts (backend notification API routes). Claims run spec by spec, then the support code's facts the specs do not assert, then gaps: the organisation picker has a page object but no spec in this slice, sort order and the empty dashboard are not proven end to end, and the INS dashboard's no-results state and columns are not asserted.
Part 5, Address book: Part 5, Address book (repos/trade-imports-ins-tests at 3c7ea8a). Read in full: the 7 animals address-book specs under tests/animals/e2e/features/address-book (address-book-navigation 1 test, addresses-add-handshake 2, addresses-copied 4, addresses-edit 6, addresses-picker 1, addresses-read-only 3 test bodies, one of them parameterised over the 5 party roles so 11 cases, addresses-submit-freeze 2); the 7 INS address-book specs under tests/ins/e2e/features/address-book (address-book 1, address-book-add-handshake-guard 1, address-book-auth 2, address-book-cross-user-visibility 1, address-book-delete 2, address-book-edit 2, address-book-persistence 1); the animals page objects addresses-page, party-picker-page, party-edit-page and contact-address-page (plus the role/slug/heading wiring in page-objects/animals/index.ts and the Address book and Dashboard link locators in page-objects/shared/base-page.ts, looked up to name what the specs click); the INS address-book page objects list, view, add, edit, delete and the shared form page; the shared E2E address-book fixtures (domain/shared/fixtures/e2e-address-book.ts); the Mongo address document model; and the address-book HTTP API client. Covered: the Consignment addresses hub and its per-role Add / Change / Edit details links; the five party pickers (page size, view details, search, newest-first pagination, no-JS selection carried across pages, Add a new address link and its stub-mode absence); the copy-not-link rule for picked addresses (book edits and soft deletes never reach a draft, a submitted notification or an amendment); the per-notification Edit address details form (labels, hint, prefill, validation messages, cancel return, isolation from the book and other notifications) for party roles and the contact address; the review-page error for a copied address that breaks the notification's rules and how it blocks continue and submit; the add handshake from the journey to the INS add page and back, its cancel path and its journey-type guard; navigation between the animals dashboard and the INS address book; and the INS address book's list, add, edit (full replace), delete (soft, confirmed), sign-in redirect, organisation-wide visibility, persistence and stored fields. Page-object-only surfaces no spec exercises (the INS view page, the list empty state, the standalone add cancel, INS form validation) are recorded as inferred or gap.
Part 6, Accessibility and security: Part 6, Accessibility and security. Read in full: tests/animals/a11y (README.md and 10 specs, 13 tests: journey initial load 1, after input 1, with errors 1, conditional pages 2, dashboard views 3 of which pagination is skipped without a second page, dashboard viewports 1, view states 1, lifecycle states 1, address edit 1, sign-in 1); fixtures/a11y.ts and utils/a11y-utils.ts (the WCAG 2.2 AA standard, axe tags, scan viewports, exclusions mechanism, failure and artefact rules, timeout); tests/animals/security (8 frontend specs, 9 tests: auth, change context, conditional pages, dashboard parameters, documents, draft validation error, lifecycle x2, submitted journey); tests/animals/security/backend/notification-submission.spec.ts (1 test); tests/ins/security/address-book (2 specs, 2 tests: auth and address book lifecycle); fixtures/security.ts (backend API client routed through the ZAP proxy); docs/security.md (ZAP DAST profiles, lanes, scanned and unscanned services, gating). tests/ins/a11y holds only .gitkeep, recorded as a gap. claims.statement: Security testing is a dynamic scan (DAST) through an OWASP ZAP proxy, with Playwright driving real authenticated journeys through it rather than ZAP crawling.

claims.statement: Security coverage is traffic-driven: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan, so the active corpus is curated by hand to drive every route worth attacking.
claims.quote: Coverage is therefore **traffic-driven**: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan. That is why the `@active` corpus is curated by hand rather than generated.

claims.statement: The passive security profile runs the e2e suite (excluding @active) through ZAP without attacking; the active profile runs only the @active suite and attacks, and is for docker-compose only.
